title: Playing with Sinatra from 1952: Wee Hours
summary: His first Los Angeles date was with Nelson Riddle, then Sinatra's comeback album Wee Hours; Edison calls him a perfectionist and gentleman.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: But it was really Nelson Riddle who started you,
Oh, yes, my first record date out here was with Nelson Riddle, you know. And then after that, I started

I started playing with Frank Sinatra in 1952. And the first album I made with him was "Wee Hours". That was on his comeback, you know. Comeback at that time. His popularity had diminished. I don't know for what reason but he hadn't sang in a long time, you know. He'd been active in the movies and --
His popularity on records, you mean?
Yes. He hadn't made any records in a long time, you know. So that "Wee Hours", with Nelson Riddle, that was a small band. And to me that's the best album he's made. Just beautiful.

Oh, yes, yes. He's such a good -- such a talent, you know, such a grand, magnificent man. Magnificent guy. He is just absolutely one of the greatest, one of the finest, finest guys that a man can have for a friend.
That's right, he's a good friend.
Now, what sort of enemy is he?
Well, I wouldn't know because we have never had any cause to be enemies.
Because we've always been good friends and --
Everything I've heard about him has been good but very often when you get somebody like that, there's --

Well, he's done what he wants, you know. And he's a perfectionist when it comes to making records. And he is, you know. And he's a fair guy, you know. And I haven't ever been in an occasion when he was any other way but a gentleman. Fantastic guy.
Well, what happens with the press, I mean --

Well, they get on anybody's nose, you know. Because the first thing they want to do is pry in your private life, you know. That's none of their business, you know, instead of asking about the business at hand. If you're a performer, that's what they ought to ask about, you know. But your private life is your own.
